findings.evidence: "This workspace holds 4 projects, synced last week." followed by a list containing only three items (Holiday Campaign Assets, Support Backlog Triage, Mobile App Revamp)
findings.fix: either display all 4 projects, or if this list is only a recent subset, label it "Recent projects" and add a "View all projects" link.
findings.location: workspace-overview section, the summary paragraph and the project list beneath it
findings.violation: the stated project count does not match the number of items actually shown, and there is no control to view the missing fourth project or the full list.

findings.fix: add visible label text or an icon inside the button (for example "Duplicate") that matches the aria-label.
findings.violation: the button has no visible text or icon inside it, only an aria-label, so a sighted user has no way to see that the control exists or what it does.

findings.evidence: both are type="submit" buttons with no linked confirmation screen, unlike the invite-member and archive-confirm flows, which each navigate to a dedicated confirmation section after saving.
findings.fix: add a confirmation state or inline success message after these two save actions, matching the pattern already used for invite-member and archive-confirm.
findings.location: project-settings section, Save button (id="project-settings-save-btn") and notification-settings section, Save button (id="notification-settings-save-btn")
findings.violation: saving a project name or a notification preference gives the user no feedback that the change succeeded, which is inconsistent with the confirmation pattern used elsewhere in the same workspace.

findings.evidence: the form's "Save" submit button (id="invite-member-save-btn") sits alongside a separate "Continue" link (id="invite-member-continue-link") that points to #invite-sent
findings.fix: combine these into one action, for example making "Save" itself submit and advance to the confirmation screen, or relabel the second control to make clear it is a distinct step.
findings.violation: it is unclear whether "Save" sends the invite or "Continue" does; having two separate controls for what appears to be a single action is confusing.

findings.evidence: "An invite was sent to the address entered above. It expires in 5 days if not accepted."
findings.fix: show the actual email address on the confirmation screen, for example "An invite was sent to jane@example.com," instead of referring to "above."
findings.violation: this confirmation screen does not display the email address, and "above" is misleading because the address was entered on a previous screen that is no longer visible.

findings.evidence: "You can restore it at any time from the archived projects list."
findings.fix: add an archived-projects view (or a link to one) so users can actually restore an archived project, or remove the claim if that destination does not exist.
findings.violation: no "archived projects list" exists anywhere in this document; there is no link or section a user can reach to view or restore an archived project.

findings.evidence: "Rows 35, 71, 78, and 83 were skipped; every other row was imported."
findings.fix: add a link or control to view or download the skipped rows, or to re-run the import after fixing them, instead of only stating the row numbers.
findings.violation: the message cites specific row numbers but gives the user no way to view, export, or fix the skipped rows, leaving this screen a dead end with no actionable next step.
